text:
Olivia - Support: heads up — we got an enterprise escalation after today's internal load run. customer saw a cascade of 429s + a few 401s during the burst window, plus elevated p95 latency. I'm attaching logs we captured in thread.

Nate SRE: ack. can you paste the root repro steps and which api key was used? did this use the shared internal key or per-team keys?

Olivia - Support: repro was our k6 run from `perf/load-scenarios/burst-ramp.js` at ~11:40 UTC. used `internal-qa-key-3` (shared). steps: ramp to 1200 rps over 90s, hold 60s, drop. We started seeing 429s ~30s into the hold. Also saw intermittent 401s for the same key. snippet from support logs: 

```
[11:41:12] POST /v1/chat 200 120ms
[11:41:27] POST /v1/chat 429 14ms - {"error":"rate_exceeded","message":"requests per minute exceeded"}
[11:41:32] POST /v1/chat 401 8ms - {"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"token revoked"}
[11:41:45] POST /v1/chat 500 3s - "timeout while waiting for worker"
```

Olivia - Support: response headers included `Retry-After: 15` on the 429s. user complained API returned 401s in the same window which looks like our rotate/revoke path was triggered by billing or auth guard. billing-bot later posted a charge error around same time.

billing-bot: automatic alert — invoice attempt failed for acct r_12345 at 11:41:30 UTC (card declined).

Tara (ops): if the key was shared we probably hit global quota and then the billing/revocation job saw a failed charge and marked the account which could cause token invalidation. that could explain the 401s. but the 429s are rate handling. we need to separate two issues: (1) burst/rate policy sizing and (2) key lifecycle reaction to billing.

Mike H: adding some metrics i pulled from the run (prometheus p90/p95):
- request rate peaked 1180 rps for ~70s
- backend p95 (inference) jumped from 230ms -> 1.6s during the peak
- our edge queue latency p95 hit 2.3s
- 429 fraction peaked at 12% of requests during burst hold

Nate SRE: thanks. two quick asks to reproduce and triage: (A) can we run the same scenario but with a non-shared dedicated key so we isolate global quota vs per-key bucket? (B) can we re-run with smaller bursts and capture token-bucket metrics (leaky_bucket_tokens, last_refill_ts)?

Olivia - Support: yes. i'll schedule both repros. quick note — the current per-key bucket config in prod is a token-bucket with `rate = 600 rpm`, `burst_capacity = 3000 tokens`, and `refill_interval = 1s` (iirc). seems like the internal run overwhelmed the shared key because of concurrency patterns.

Tara (ops): those numbers might be the problem. 600 rpm = 10 rps baseline but burst_capacity 3000 lets short spikes go huge. for internal defaults we should move to a more conservative base and limit burst multiplier. proposal: default per-key rate = 1200 rpm (20 rps) for paid keys, 120 rpm (2 rps) for free; burst multiplier = 3x sustained for max 30s; burst credit window = 30s. that means paid burst capacity ~3600 tokens, enforced with a sliding window cap to avoid unlimited short bursts stacking.

Nate SRE: I'd rather a token bucket with two-stage limits: per-second smoothing (max instantaneous concurrency) + per-minute quota (RPM). Practical default: per-second max = 200 rps per key for paid; rpm = 6000; burst_tokens = min( per_second_max * 10, rpm * 0.5 ). Example: if per_second_max=200 => burst_tokens = min(2000, 3000) = 2000. and an explicit `burst_window_seconds = 20`. That prevents 1-off huge absorb.

Olivia - Support: sounds reasonable. can we also add a protection so shared internal keys have stricter caps by default? those shared keys keep biting us.

Tara (ops): yes — policy: any key tagged `internal_shared` gets enforced caps of 1/10th paid rate and no burst by default, unless you opt-in. we'll add guardrails in the admin console.

Mike H: re: the 401s — i dug into the auth logs. sequence looks like: 1) run triggers rate limit and some backend timeouts 2) billing charge fails, 3) account enters `delinquent` state, 4) revocation job revokes tokens, causing 401s. so support saw 401s because revocation was synchronous during the experiment. we should ensure revocation is async/queued-with-delay for active requests to avoid mass 401s during transient failures.

Olivia - Support: action items for support runbook: 1) when customer reports combined 429+401, check billing state first (`/admin/accounts/:id/billing`), 2) check key tags (shared vs per-team), 3) look at token-bucket metrics, 4) ask for replay logs and k6 script. i'll draft a KB.

Nate SRE: technical action items for infra:
- add a non-shared repro harness: CLI snippet to run k6 against a single key:
```
k6 run --vus 600 --duration 2m perf/load-scenarios/burst-ramp.js --env API_KEY=sk-repro-XXX
```
- capture these metrics in the run: `token_bucket_tokens`, `token_bucket_last_refill`, `edge_queue_len`, `upstream_latency_ms`.
- add an alert: 429_rate > 5% for 5m => paging.
- adjust default per-key policy in staging to the two-stage limit above and run comparative runs.

Tara (ops): I'll open a PR to the rate-limiter config repo with proposed defaults and gating tests that run the k6 scenario at PR time (smoke). PR will include a YAML snippet with defaults. sample yaml (inline):
```
policies:
  per_key:
    paid:
      rpm: 6000
      per_second_max: 200
      burst_window_seconds: 20
      burst_multiplier: 3
    free:
      rpm: 120
      per_second_max: 5
      burst_multiplier: 1
  internal_shared_override:
    enabled: true
    rpm_factor: 0.1
    allow_burst: false
```

Mike H: tiny note — keep `Retry-After` semantics stable. SDKs should respect `Retry-After` header and exponential backoff for 429. also return structured error JSON with `code` + `retry_after_seconds` so we can programmatically route.

Olivia - Support: i'll add that to the KB and update support playbook templates. also will attach the failing run artifacts to the escalation ticket and notify the customer that we're updating rate-limiter defaults and will run a controlled replay before rolling.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: PR #452-rate-limiter-defaults -> staging (CI checks running).

Nate SRE: next steps for me: run the dedicated-key repro this afternoon at 18:00 UTC with the new default policy in a branch. i'll post the k6 run id and raw metrics. Olivia/Tara — please confirm the support KB and the PR respectively so we can coordinate the staging run.

Olivia - Support: confirmed. i'll update customer and tag them for a controlled replay next week. thanks team :thumbsup:

Tara (ops): leaving a note — we should publish a short internal note reminding folks not to use shared keys for stress tests. will put it in #eng-sre and #devex.

Mike H: nice — after staging runs, let's pick conservative prod rollout: 10% traffic -> 30% -> 100% with canary monitors on 429 and 401 rates.

Olivia - Support: agreed. i'll add that to the escalation ticket.

Nate SRE: closing the loop — i'll post results and any follow-up fixes in this thread.

[thread end]
